First, decree that T(1,1) = 1. Then for n > 0, let S(n) = {(i,j) : 1 <= i <= n, 1 <= j <= n}, and let T(1,n+1) = least positive integer not among T(i,j) for (i,j) in S(n); T(n+1,1) = least positive integer not among T(i,j) for (i,j) in S(n) and not (T,n+1); T(m,n+1) = T(m,1)*T(1,n+1). These rules generate an array T which starts out like this: T = [ [1, 2, 4, 7, 9, 13, 15, 18, 23, 25, 29], [3, 6, 12, 21, 27, 39, 45, 54, 69, 75, 87], [5, 10, 20, 35, 45, 65, 75, 90, 115, 125, 145], [8, 16, 32, 56, 72, 104, 120, 144, 184, 200, 232], [11, 22, 44, 77, 99, 143, 165, 198, 253, 275, 319] ] Every prime is in row 1 of T or column 1, but not both. The difference sequence of row 1 starts with 1,2,3,2,4,2,3,5,2,4,2,5,4,2,4,3,2,4,3,2,2,4,4,7,2,3,2,4,3,5,5,3,4. Here's the problem: prove (or disprove) that this difference sequence bounded. More terms of the array T and its first row are given at A129258 and A129259.
